state.description: The default view. A mono chain with three tone blocks (drive pedal, amp, cab IR) and two open + slots. Input/output meters flank the gallery; the faceplate carries global gain, gate and tone stack; the hint bar sits at the bottom.
state.title: Signal chain - mono

state.description: Input at 0 dBFS latches the clip LED (topmost dot) red; the output column lights to -3. Hovering the lit LED shows the clip hint; clicking it clears the latch.
state.title: Signal chain - hot meters (clip latched)

state.description: A fresh instance before any tone is loaded: five empty + slots. Clicking any + opens the Default browser (signing in first if needed).
state.title: Signal chain - empty

state.description: Clicking a tile opens the block detail takeover: artwork, model picker with prev/next, In/Out/Mix knobs, per-block meters, and the header row with EQ, share, swap, power and remove. This NAM block carries calibration metadata (gauge next to the title).
state.title: Block detail card

state.description: The (i) view: the artwork shrinks beside the title column and the Default description (clamped, MORE expands), gear makes and tags load underneath; the card grows past the fixed height and the column scrolls to the faceplate.
state.title: Block detail - info view

state.description: Signed out, the info view has no catalog to read from: a Log In prompt replaces the description, and the model picker is disabled with a sign-in hint.
state.title: Block detail - info view, signed out

state.description: The per-block 6-band EQ opened from the detail card, in the gain-only fader view. The EQ pill in the header shows an outline when the EQ is actively shaping the sound.
state.title: Block EQ - slider view

state.description: The same EQ in the parametric curve view: draggable band dots over the live output spectrum, with freq/gain/Q chips per band.
state.title: Block EQ - curve view

state.description: The model dropdown on the detail card, paging through every model of the tone from the Default catalog. Signed-out users see the picker disabled with a sign-in hint instead.
state.title: Block detail - model picker open

state.description: Stereo mode: channel 0 feeds the Left lane, channel 1 the Right lane. Each lane has its own pan knob on the rail between them (linkable), and the faceplate gains Balance, Offset and the input-mode button.
state.title: Signal chain - stereo, independent lanes

state.description: A branch: the Right lane taps its input from the Left lane after the amp block (elbow + indent). Used for wet/dry rigs and parallel cab setups. Clicking the junction makes the chains independent again.
state.title: Signal chain - stereo, branched

state.description: The chromatic tuner replaces the middle band (toggled from the header). With no input signal the note readout and bars sit dimmed.
state.title: Tuner - no signal

state.description: Within +-5 cents both center bars and both triangles light up blue.
state.title: Tuner - in tune

state.description: Flat notes light the left bars; the further off, the more bars.
state.title: Tuner - flat

state.description: Sharp notes light the right bars.
state.title: Tuner - sharp

state.description: Sharps hang the accidental off the right of the letter so the letter stays centered.
state.title: Tuner - accidental

state.description: The tuner reads the signal before the pitch shift, so an in-tune low E string still shows E. The shift is two semitones down, so a small line under the frequency reads Sounds as D.
state.title: Tuner with a pitch shift

state.description: A tile while its model file downloads from Default: loading dots over the artwork. The second block here is mid-download; audio passes through until the model is ready.
state.title: Block downloading (gallery)

state.description: The same download state on the open detail card.
state.title: Block downloading (detail card)

state.description: The failed state on the detail card. Retry re-queues the download; when signed in the session token is refreshed first.
state.title: Block download failed (detail card)

state.description: Clicking any internet-dependent action (+ slot, swap, login) with no network interface up opens this gate. It is an instant navigator.onLine check; a connected-but-dead network instead lands on the failed-download / OAuth recovery paths.
state.title: Offline modal

state.description: No network, but every model in the chain is already downloaded: the rig keeps playing normally. Tone artwork cannot be fetched, so tiles fall back to their gear-type icons; everything else works until an action needs the internet.
state.title: Offline with cached models

state.description: The sign-in screen the instant a login hands off to the system browser (Select Tone mockup 13342:46017): a full page in the tone browser's slot with a bare ← to abandon it, the loading dots over "Sign in with your browser", and under them the ways round a browser that may not have opened: "Browser didn't open? Copy link to sign in, then return here." with the Copy Link button (the authorize URL, for any browser on this machine), and the grey "Sign in on a different device" link to the device-flow page. The browser path stays live throughout.
state.title: Sign in - waiting on the browser

state.description: The launcher itself refused to open the browser: the copy says so and leads with the fallbacks. (A browser that starts and then dies, as Chromium does under root on Linux, reports nothing, which is why the fallbacks are always on the page.)
state.title: Sign in - browser could not be opened

state.description: Copy Link puts the authorize URL on the clipboard and reads Copied for two seconds.
state.title: Sign in - link copied

drives.target: Sign in on a different device

state.description: Sign in on a different device asks Default for a device code (POST /oauth/device_authorization): the dots while it answers.
state.title: Sign in - phone: getting a code

drives.target: Sign in on a different device

state.description: The device flow (RFC 8628; Select Tone mockup 13342:46055): "Sign in on your phone" over two cards with OR between them, a QR code of verification_uri_complete for the phone's camera, and for anyone who cannot scan, "Visit fixtures.invalid/activate, sign in, and enter this code:" over the user code (the address underlined to read as one, not a link). The plugin polls the token endpoint at the server's interval until the code is approved; finishing in the browser still works meanwhile.
state.title: Sign in - phone: scan or type the code

drives.target: Sign in on a different device

state.description: The code went unused for its ten minutes (or was declined, or Default would not issue one): the reason, with New code for a fresh one and Copy Link still to hand.
state.title: Sign in - phone: code expired

state.description: Landing back from fixtures.invalid with an authorization code: the sign-in screen stays up over the chain while the tokens are exchanged.
state.title: OAuth - returning from Default

state.description: A sign-in that failed (the browser came back with an error, or the token exchange did): the reason on the sign-in screen with Try again / Dismiss in place of the dots; ← dismisses too.
state.title: Sign in - failed

version.message_html: New in 1.5.0: per-block EQ curve view, stereo chain branching, and lower CPU on Apple Silicon.

state.description: Startup update check against the Default version endpoint (best effort, never blocks). Remind me later snoozes for 1/7/30 days; the update also stays visible in Settings while snoozed.
state.title: Update available

state.description: macOS privacy is blocking audio input entirely; the device opens but the stream is silent. Highest priority and not dismissable; the action jumps to the OS privacy page.
state.title: Banner - microphone access denied

state.description: No input device selected (or no active input channel): the plugin cannot hear the instrument.
state.title: Banner - no audio input

state.description: Same rule as no-input, but the wording flips when the device failed to open or was unplugged.
state.title: Banner - device disconnected

state.description: A device is open but nothing is routed out, so the plugin is inaudible.
state.title: Banner - no audio output

state.description: Hear Yourself is off while an input is active, so the user hears nothing.
state.title: Banner - input muted (by the user)

state.description: The app auto-muted because a microphone is feeding speakers; different copy pointing at headphones/interface.
state.title: Banner - input muted to prevent feedback

state.description: Monitoring is on with a mic-into-speakers setup: nothing is muted but a squeal is one gain bump away. Dismissable.
state.title: Banner - feedback risk

state.description: An ASIO driver reports devices while a slower Windows driver type is current.
state.title: Banner - ASIO available (Windows)

state.description: Buffer above 512 samples with a smaller option available: nudges toward a more responsive setting.
state.title: Banner - large buffer latency

state.description: Informational, lowest priority: off 48 kHz the chain resamples and burns a little more CPU.
state.title: Banner - not running at 48 kHz

state.description: The Select tone screen: search box, the filter button, the verified and Profile chips, and the gear chips over the trending catalog.
state.title: Tone browser - search (signed in)

state.description: Sort set to Newest, its menu reopened, then the chip's × pressed: the sort is back to Trending and the menu is gone; any filter change closes an open menu.
state.title: Tone browser - clearing a chip closes its open menu

state.description: The ← row zooms with the window; everything under it does not. The search box, filter row and cards keep their 1x height and widen to fill the column, so the bigger window shows more of the page.
state.title: Tone browser - window at 1.3x, the body holds 1x

state.description: Once three cards fit at their default width (800 x 1.6 = 1280 >= 3 x 392 + 2 x 16) the grid goes three-up.
state.title: Tone browser - window at 1.6x, three columns

state.description: A popover takes its anchor's scale: the Sort menu opened from the 1x filter row is 1x too, sitting under its chip.
state.title: Tone browser - window at 1.6x, a filter menu

state.description: Searching needs a session; signed out, the screen previews Default's trending feed instead (GET /tones/trending takes no token): the gear chips alone over the cards, with a sign-in CTA at the foot of the list. A card leads to the sign-in page.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: trending preview

state.description: Signed out, a gear chip narrows the trending feed to that type (the endpoint's one filter); the active chip reads white. The pick carries into the search once signed in.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: gear chip

state.description: Signed out with a gear the trending feed has nothing for (Spaces): the empty copy under the chips, the CTA still on offer.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: no trending tones of a type

state.description: Scrolled to the foot of the trending cards: the Default mark, "Discover a zillion more tones." and the sign-in button, which starts the browse-intent OAuth flow.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: the CTA under the list

state.description: Signed out, a card opens the sign-in page: the bare ← (back to the cards) and the centred prompt, whose button starts the browse-intent OAuth flow.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: a card clicked

drives.target: Sign in or create free account

state.description: The card page's CTA starts the browse-intent login: the same sign-in screen takes over the browser (← returns to it), and a finished sign-in lands back on the browser signed in.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: signing in

drives.target: Sign in or create free account

state.description: The CTA runs the browse-intent login and lands back on this same screen signed in: the search box and the full filter row appear in place, a gear pick made while signed out still applies, and the trending cards give way to the search.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: signed in from the CTA

state.description: The loading dots under the gear chips while the trending feed is in flight.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: loading

state.description: The trending feed failed (Default unreachable, 5xx): the error copy plus Try again under the gear chips.
state.title: Tone browser - signed out: trending failed

state.description: The loading dots while the first search is in flight and there is nothing to keep on screen.
state.title: Tone browser - loading

state.description: A search with no results: the empty copy under the untouched filters.
state.title: Tone browser - nothing found

state.description: A failed search (Default unreachable, 5xx): error copy plus Try again.
state.title: Tone browser - search failed

state.description: After clicking a card the grid dims and the card gets a busy overlay while the tone and its first model resolve; the tone then lands in the chain.
state.title: Tone browser - loading a picked tone

state.description: The grid scrolled most of a row: cards run into a solid band of black under the pills, then fade out fast, so they never look like they touch the filters.
state.title: Tone browser - results scrolled under the filter row

state.description: Enter submits the text; the × on the right clears it and submits again.
state.title: Tone browser - search text

state.description: A gear chip narrows the catalog to that type; the active chip reads white.
state.title: Tone browser - gear chip

state.description: The verified chip keeps only tones from verified creators (badge beside their names).
state.title: Tone browser - verified creators

state.description: The Profile chip lists the signed-in user's own streams: Recently used, Favorites, Created.
state.title: Tone browser - Profile menu

state.description: A profile filter set: the chip shows it with an ×, and the catalog-only filters park (those streams take a title search and gear alone; the search box stays live).
state.title: Tone browser - Recently used

state.description: Recently used with "vox" typed: the stream endpoints take a title search, so the box narrows the user's own list; gear chips still apply, the parked filters don't.
state.title: Tone browser - Search within a profile

state.description: Favorites with no tones yet (fresh account): stream-specific empty copy.
state.title: Tone browser - empty profile stream

state.description: The filter button unfolds the catalog filters (sort, format, tags, makes, creators, calibrated) ahead of the rest of the row.
state.title: Tone browser - more filters

state.description: The Sort chip's menu: Trending, Popular, Newest, Oldest (Best match joins while there is search text). The sort in force reads white, no check; Trending is the default, so the chip stays gray on it.
state.title: Tone browser - Sort menu

state.description: A format picked: the chip shows it with an × and the results narrow to impulse responses.
state.title: Tone browser - Format: IR

state.description: A taxonomy menu: a search field over the most-used names from the API.
state.title: Tone browser - Tags menu

state.description: A pick closes the menu and narrows the results; reopened, the chosen tags lead the list ticked. The chip lists them with an ×.
state.title: Tone browser - tags picked

state.description: Newest picked: the Sort chip names it in white with an × back to the default, and the filters button would carry the dot once folded.
state.title: Tone browser - Sort set

state.description: Cabinet picked with the filters expanded: cabinets are impulse responses with no calibration data, so the Calibrated chip dims and the flag is left out of the request. The divider parts the extra filters from the ones always shown.
state.title: Tone browser - Calibrated parked under IR gear

state.description: Both formats read gray until one is picked; the panel is wide enough for the full names.
state.title: Tone browser - Format menu

state.description: Creator rows lead with the avatar (the person glyph when there is none), as on the cards.
state.title: Tone browser - Creators menu

state.description: Leave with a gear chip set and come back: the query, filter row and results are retained for the session, with no fetch.
state.title: Tone browser - back where it was left

state.description: Back from the catalog filters with some set: the filter button reads white with a dot.
state.title: Tone browser - filters set, collapsed

version.message_html: New in 1.5.0: per-block EQ curve view, stereo chain branching, and lower CPU on Apple Silicon.

state.description: Hosted builds get a single page: Show Info Bar, Show Gate and Show Pitch Shift view toggles (gate on, pitch off by default; a powered effect shows regardless), MIDI Mapping and Advanced entry points, the update row when a newer version exists, and the running version in the footer.
state.title: Plugin Settings (in a DAW)

state.description: NAM A2 size (LITE/FULL), per-block normalization, input calibration with its dBu field, oversampling with rate picker, multi-core stereo, and diagnostics (copy/reveal logs).
state.title: Plugin Settings - Advanced

state.description: No mappings yet: explainer copy plus the control picker.
state.title: MIDI Mapping - empty

state.description: Learned CC/note assignments with re-learn / remove buttons, a channel filter, and a target armed for learn waiting for the next hardware move (or a typed CC number).
state.title: MIDI Mapping - mappings + learn armed

state.description: The target picker open: every mappable control with its context (presets, global knobs, and a power toggle per chain slot named after the tone currently in it). Picking one arms learn.
state.title: MIDI Mapping - choosing a control

state.description: The Presets section between MIDI Mapping and Diagnostics: a link that opens the user presets folder in the OS file browser.
state.title: Presets

state.description: The standalone app adds this tab: driver/device pickers, input channel selection with live meters, Hear Yourself, test tone, buffer and sample rate, and MIDI hardware inputs.
state.title: System Settings (standalone)

state.description: The banner rules render inline in the settings form too: here the mic-permission error with its Allow Access action.
state.title: System Settings - mic access denied

state.description: Hear Yourself is on with a mic-into-speakers setup, so the feedback warning renders inline under the toggle that causes it (same copy as the main-window banner).
state.title: System Settings - feedback risk

state.description: The auto-mute state inline: Hear Yourself is off because a microphone is feeding speakers, with the copy pointing at headphones or an interface.
state.title: System Settings - input muted to prevent feedback

state.description: Scrolled down to Buffer Size / Sample Rate / MIDI Inputs. Running off 48 kHz puts the informational rate notice inline under the picker.
state.title: System Settings - sample rate warning

state.description: A saved publishable key: the page says so and offers Remove key. It never shows the key.
state.title: System Settings - saved key

state.description: The switch for the daily update check, on when the user never set it, and its one help line. The check asks GitHub once a day and sends no account data.
state.title: System Settings - update check

state.description: Hamburger + avatar pill; signed out it offers Settings and Login.
state.title: Account menu - signed out

state.description: Signed in the avatar comes from the Default profile and Logout replaces Login.
state.title: Account menu - signed in

state.description: A build with no key: Login opens the page that takes a publishable key.
state.title: Key page

state.description: The key page after a save of a value that is not a publishable key: an inline error, and nothing saved.
state.title: Key page - not a key

state.description: Saving stores the whole chain + faceplate under a name; a same-name user preset is overwritten.
state.title: Preset save popover

state.description: Factory (Default) and user sections with search; user presets get rename/delete on hover, and the reorder toggle swaps those for move up/down.
state.title: Preset browser

state.description: The app-wide toast pill above the faceplate; also used for Link Copied (share), and the auto-measure results.
state.title: Toast - Preset Saved

state.description: In mono, Spread doubles the chain into an ADT-style stereo image: the faceplate group expands to Offset + Wobble knobs, power button, and the mono-safety correlation LED. The output meter and Balance switch to their stereo forms.
state.title: Spread enabled (mono)

state.description: Right-clicking the Gate group (knob or power) opens the gate deck above the plate, anchored to the knob: Release, Hold and Range knobs, no power switches. Every knob sits at its default (50 ms, 20 ms, 80 dB), so a stock rig reads unchanged.
state.title: Gate advanced deck

state.description: Right-clicking the Pitch group (knob or power) opens the pitch deck above the plate, anchored to the knob: the STEP toggle (armed: whole semitones), Tonality and Buffer knobs, no power switches. The group is powered so the knob reads lit; every deck control sits at its default (STEP on, Off, 30 ms), so a stock rig reads unchanged.
state.title: Pitch advanced deck

state.description: Right-clicking the Pitch knob opens the pitch deck with the tuning pickers. The instrument is the default six-string guitar and the shift is two semitones down, so the tuning picker reads D Standard (-2) and the string strip reads E→D A→G D→C G→F B→A e→d above the STEP, Tonality and Buffer row.
state.title: Pitch deck with a tuning

state.description: The pitch deck with the five-string bass picked on this machine. The shift is two semitones down, so the tuning picker reads A Standard (-2) and the string strip names the five bass strings B→A E→D A→G D→C G→F.
state.title: Pitch deck on a five-string bass

state.description: The pitch deck on a four-string bass with OPTIMIZE on, its default with no stored value. The shift is two semitones down, so the tuning picker reads D Standard (-2). The OPTIMIZE toggle beside STEP is lit, and the Buffer knob shows the 40 ms window that the policy keeps for a bass.
state.title: Pitch deck with OPTIMIZE on

state.description: The pitch deck on the default six-string guitar with OPTIMIZE off, a stored value of false. The shift is two semitones down, so the tuning picker reads D Standard (-2). The OPTIMIZE toggle beside STEP is dark, and the Buffer knob keeps the 30 ms window that the player set.
state.title: Pitch deck with OPTIMIZE off

state.description: The pitch deck on the default six-string guitar with OPTIMIZE on, its default with no stored value. A stream runs with a buffer of 64 frames, and the engine estimates a delay of 16 ms from the input to the output. The readout ~16 ms shows under the OPTIMIZE toggle. The shift is two semitones down, so the tuning picker reads D Standard (-2).
state.title: Pitch deck with the delay

state.description: The pitch shift is on at two semitones down on a six-string guitar, so the caption under the Pitch knob on the bottom bar reads D Std instead of Pitch. No deck is open.
state.title: Pitch knob with a tuning caption

state.description: Right-clicking the Spread group opens the shared deck panel above the plate: Wobble and Crossover knobs with their power buttons, the Diffuse power, and the mono-safety correlation LED. Spread defaults every section on.
state.title: Spread advanced deck

state.description: With Align off, right-clicking the ALIGN advert still opens its deck, flush-right to the group. Align defaults every section off, so the knobs render dimmed.
state.title: Align advanced deck (advert state)

state.description: Clicking the auto button next to Balance arms a ~2 s measurement: the pinned Listening toast stays up while the user plays, then the matched trim lands as a toast.
state.title: Auto-balance listening

state.description: With a real stereo source feeding the plugin, the faceplate input button picks what enters the chain: both channels summed, each channel through its own copy of the chain (Dual Mono), or left/right mirrored onto both. Session state, not preset state.
state.title: Input mode menu

state.description: A mono chain on a stereo track with Dual Mono selected: each channel runs the chain on its own. The input button shows the stereo glyph in its engaged fill, the output meter splits into L/R, Balance and Auto Balance appear to trim the two voices, and Spread dims with its reason (the chain already outputs two real channels).
state.title: Dual mono

state.description: Right-clicking a tone tile offers Copy (tone, model and all settings); right-clicking a + slot offers Paste when a copied block is on the clipboard.
state.title: Tile context menu

state.description: The info bar can be turned off (X on the bar or the Settings toggle); the window shrinks by its height rather than stretching the UI.
state.title: Hint bar hidden
